security_audit.summary: All 175 static findings were adjudicated as false positives after contextual review. The flagged patterns are PyTorch model evaluation methods, Markdown formatting, dataset cache paths, dictionary key iteration, explicit output generation, imports, and official PyG URLs. No prompt injection, secret access, exfiltration intent, or covert command execution was found.

static_findings.snippet: 2. **Citation networks**: Planetoid datasets are perfect for node classification
PyG represents graphs using the `torch_geometric.data.Data` class with these key attributes:
- **`data.edge_index`**: Graph connectivity in COO format `[2, num_edges]`
- **`data.y`**: Target labels for nodes or graphs
Edges are stored in COO (coordinate) format as a `[2, num_edges]` tensor:
- A `batch` vector maps each node to its source graph
- **`message()`**: Constructs messages from source to target nodes
**Variable naming convention**: Appending `_i` or `_j` to tensor names automatically maps them to ta

content.user_title: Build Graph Neural Networks with PyTorch Geometric
content.value_statement: Graph learning projects require careful choices for data, models, sampling, and evaluation. This skill provides PyTorch Geometric guidance, examples, templates, benchmarks, and visualization utilities.
actual_capabilities: Explains PyTorch Geometric data structures, batching, message passing, transforms, pooling, and heterogeneous graphs.
Provides patterns for GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE, GIN, custom layers, and graph classifiers.
Generates Python training templates for supported node and graph classification models.
Benchmarks GCN, GAT, and GraphSAGE models on supported PyG datasets.
Visualizes graph structure, degree distributions, and summary statistics with NetworkX and Matplotlib.
Catalogs PyG datasets, convolution layers, aggregation operators, and graph transforms.
limitations: Generated templates cover GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE, and GIN, not every PyG architecture.
Benchmark scripts use simple training splits and do not provide production experiment tracking.
Dataset examples use shared temporary directories and may download substantial files.
Two referenced documents, layer_capabilities.md and api_patterns.md, are not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Prototype a node classifier
use_cases.description: Select a PyG layer, load a citation dataset, and create a training workflow with evaluation masks.

use_cases.title: Compare GNN baselines
use_cases.description: Run repeated benchmarks for GCN, GAT, and GraphSAGE on a supported dataset.

use_cases.title: Inspect graph data
use_cases.description: Visualize graph topology, degree patterns, labels, and basic statistics before model development.

prompt_templates.title: Create a first PyG graph
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to represent my graph in PyTorch Geometric. My node features are {features}, and my edges are {edge_format}.

prompt_templates.title: Build a node classifier
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a {GCN|GAT|GraphSAGE} node-classification workflow for {dataset}. Include preprocessing, model structure, training, validation, and test evaluation.

prompt_templates.title: Scale graph training
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt my PyTorch Geometric pipeline for {node_count} nodes and {edge_count} edges. Recommend sampling, batching, memory controls, and evaluation strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Design a heterogeneous GNN
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a heterogeneous GNN for node types {node_types} and edge types {edge_types}. Specify metadata handling, relation layers, losses, and validation.

output_examples.input: I need a baseline for Cora node classification.
output: Recommended model: a two-layer GCN with dropout.
Use the provided train, validation, and test masks.
Track validation accuracy and report the selected test result.

output_examples.input: My social graph has millions of nodes and does not fit in memory.
output_examples.output: Use neighbor sampling with limited hops, seed-node loss calculation, controlled batch sizes, and validation on a stable sampling configuration.

output_examples.input: Compare GAT and GraphSAGE for a product graph.
output: GAT can model varying neighbor importance but uses more memory.
GraphSAGE is a practical baseline for sampled large graphs.
Compare both with identical splits, features, budgets, and metrics.

best_practices: Inspect feature dimensions, label shapes, edge direction, self-loops, and split masks before training.
Choose layers based on graph structure, edge features, scale, and task level.
Separate training, validation, and test evaluation, then report repeated-run statistics.
anti_patterns: Do not load large graphs fully into memory when neighbor sampling is required.
Do not compare models with different data splits, preprocessing, or evaluation metrics.
Do not assume every graph is undirected or every task uses node-level labels.

faq.question: Does this skill install PyTorch Geometric?
faq.answer: It provides installation commands, but installation requires user execution and a compatible PyTorch environment.

faq.question: Which model architectures are covered?
faq.answer: It covers GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE, GIN, custom message-passing layers, heterogeneous models, and pooling patterns.

faq.question: Can it work with custom datasets?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains InMemoryDataset, Dataset, CSV loading, preprocessing, and custom Data objects.

faq.question: Does it support large graphs?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes neighbor sampling and batching, but capacity depends on hardware, dataset size, and model design.

faq.question: Can it benchmark production models?
faq.answer: The benchmark utility provides simple baseline comparisons. It does not include distributed orchestration, experiment tracking, or exhaustive tuning.

faq.question: Will dataset examples access the network?
faq.answer: Many PyG datasets download files when missing. Review dataset sources, storage paths, licenses, and expected sizes before running examples.
